references.text: God changes Abram's name to Abraham, parallel to the name change of Sarai to Sarah in verse 15.
God confirms the promise of a son to Abraham and Sarah, and Sarah laughs at the thought because of her age.
The Lord visits Sarah as He said, and does as He promised by giving her a son. Sarah expresses joy over God's faithfulness.
Isaiah looks back on Abraham and Sarah as ancestors of God's people and as an example of God's blessing.
Paul uses the story of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory: Sarah represents the covenant of promise and the free children, while Hagar represents slavery under the law.
Peter mentions Sarah as an example of a godly woman who trusted in God and obeyed her husband Abraham.
Parallel about divine name changes that mark a new identity and covenant role for both Abraham and Jacob.
